analysis.title: UBS Cash Trading - Main Themes 2nd November
key_insights: Friday's US session closed well off the lows but below the levels seen at the European cash close. The S&P 500 fell 1.8% and the Nasdaq fell 2.9%, with the AI trade the main drag.
Semis, memory and neoclouds were all sharply lower on Friday. Big tech was broadly weaker, with NVDA down 4.2% and SPCX down 6.4%.
Early Monday shows relief. EStoxx is +20bps at the start and +90bps off Friday's lows. US futures are higher, with ESA +40bps and NQA +80bps.
Treasuries offered some offset on Friday, yields 2-8bps lower with the curve steepening further. Desk feedback says the concern is that a bid to Treasuries is starting to imply a growth scare.

In Asia, Tokyo Electron rose 6.5% after earnings, giving the semi-cap group some relief. Kioxia fell 16% on a softer outlook, roughly in line with its ADR move, which shows how high the guidance bar remains.
KOSPI is +2% near the day's highs after reversing a 2% intraday loss. National Pension cash buying is net +$190mn today after +$640mn on Friday, its largest single day of buying in nearly five years.
China is +1.1% and is looking through a soft PMI print on reports that financial regulators will meet banks and securities firms today to discuss measures to support the capital market.

Crude is optically lower by 3-3.5% on reports that President Trump wants to give Iran diplomacy more time before potentially resuming strikes after Tuesday's midterms. Reuters reports Qatari mediators are holding a third straight day of talks with Iranian representatives. Part of the move is the front month rolling from Dec26 to Jan27 (Brent $109.5, WTI $100.5).
The desk calls tomorrow's US midterms the near-term pivot for both the Iran timeline and broader risk appetite.
The desk's read is that the AI complex likely needs more than one positive print out of Tokyo to signal the derisking has run its course.

Week ahead: Monday brings global manufacturing PMIs, German retail sales, US ISM manufacturing and AAPL and PLTR earnings. Tuesday is the US midterms, the RBA decision, JOLTS and factory orders. Wednesday brings Eurozone CPI, services PMIs, US ADP and ISM services, the US Treasury quarterly refunding announcement and QCOM earnings.

Thursday is a key central bank day. The BoE decision is expected to be a 25bp hike to 4%, alongside Norges Bank, US jobless claims and speeches from Lagarde and Schnabel. Friday's US October nonfarm payrolls are expected at 65k versus 29k prior.
Other earnings this week from companies above $100bn market cap: AMD, AMGN, APO, ANET, ARM, BKNG, COIN, COP, DASH, DTE, EOG, ETN, F, FDX, ISRG, MCD, MELI, NVO, PFE, SHOP, SONY, TTE, UBER and VRTX.

European cash flow on Friday finished balanced (48/52) with participation about 20% below the YTD average. Banks (25% of turnover) were busiest, with demand in Spanish and Dutch names and supply in Italian. Healthcare (24%) saw demand in large-cap pharma. Technology (7%) was better for sale, with supply in software. Telecoms (6%) saw supply in Mobile/IT. Div Fins and Energy saw supply.
